Agenda

Presentation overview

01 · Current challenges

No single view of energy loss

01

No dedicated loss monitoring system

Loss data is scattered across different systems with no single unified view.

It is hard to pinpoint exactly where losses occur across the distribution network.

02

Limited real-time visibility

Limited ability to detect losses at feeder, transformer and customer level.

Problem-solving is reactive, after the fact, rather than preventive.

03

Manual, disconnected analysis

Analysing and reconciling data takes a long time across separate systems, which delays detecting and resolving energy loss.

TodayReactive response after incidents
With ELMSProactive detection and prevention
02 · Project objectives

Five goals for energy loss management

1More accurately calculate energy loss at each level of the network
2Separate Technical Loss from Non-Technical Loss
3Detect abnormal consumption and possible electricity theft early
4Improve the accuracy of energy loss calculation
5Support planning to improve the network and reduce losses
02 · Project objectives · Existing systems

Existing systems ELMS builds on

Integration-first approach: ELMS connects to the existing OMMD system to protect current investment and minimise disruption to operations.

01Multidrive HES

Collects Load Profile and meter data from smart meters, and records interval consumption data.

Head End System

02OMMD Middleware

Connects billing with the Head End System. Collects and standardises Load Profile data and provides secure data exchange.

Central platform

03OONE Billing

Manages customer billing, meter reading, invoices, accounts and usage history. Supplies billed energy for loss calculation.

Billed energy
03 · Solution overview

One module, one view of loss

Unified management through OMMD

ELMS is a module built inside OMMD, providing unified management and comprehensive loss monitoring across the whole network.

Automated analysis

Advanced automated analysis and near real-time monitoring detect anomalies early and continuously improve performance.

Single source of truth

Consolidated data keeps loss figures consistent across departments and supports decisions based on clear information.

03 · Solution overview · Dashboard

Dashboard and monitoring capability

Near real-time data LIVE

The dashboard instantly shows energy flow, losses and system performance at every network level.

  • Total loss and Technical / Non-Technical split
  • Energy loss analysis and trends
  • Configurable threshold alerts
  • Drill into high-loss feeders and substations
  • Drill down by area, substation, feeder or transformer

03 · Solution overview · Alerts

Alerts and operational support

Threshold-based alerts

Alerts on loss percentage and abnormal consumption. The system sends notifications instantly.

Abnormal pattern detection

Identifies unusual consumption, signs of meter tampering and network irregularities.

Operational support

Key information and prioritised alerts help field teams go on site and resolve issues on time.

05 · Key benefits

What ELMS delivers for EDC

Operational, financial and strategic benefits of the Energy Loss Management Module in OMMD.

Click to continue1 / 6
01

Improved visibility of energy losses

  • Accurate, transparent loss measurement
  • Energy balance across generation, substations and feeders
  • See where and how losses occur
02

Reduction of technical & non-technical losses

  • Early detection of abnormal loss patterns
  • Targeted corrective actions
  • Direct revenue protection and recovery
03

Enhanced operational efficiency

  • Automates manual, fragmented loss reporting
  • Centralised dashboards and alerts
  • Faster decisions and field investigations
04

Better use of existing investments

  • Maximises value of smart meters and MultiDrive HES
  • Builds on OMMD middleware and OONE Billing
  • No standalone platform needed
05

Scalable foundation

  • Ready for advanced analytics
  • Predictive loss detection
  • Supports smart grid and digital transformation
From generation to household: ELMS tracks energy flow down to each home (when data is available for calculation), identifies loss points and supports effective loss-reduction strategies.

07 · Conclusion

Conclusion

Summary of the proposed Energy Loss Management System for EDC.

A comprehensive, data-driven solution to monitor and reduce energy loss across EDC’s network.

Comprehensive monitoring and analysis of energy losses across the distribution network
Built on existing OMMD, OONE Billing and MultiDrive HES: efficient to implement, maximising current infrastructure
Tracks energy flow from generation to household (when data is available for calculation) and pinpoints loss points
Supports effective loss-reduction strategies and protects EDC revenue
→ An important step toward a more efficient, data-driven and modern electricity distribution system.
Revenue protectionSmart grid ready
